hero.title: Clean
hero.subtitle: Helping developers practice Domain-Driven Design with understandable elements and executable rules to build highly maintainable software systems.
hero.summary: A practical engineering guide that simplifies core DDD concepts, keeping complex systems clear by protecting boundaries.

definition.title: Definition of CleanDDD
definition.description: CleanDDD, short for Clean Domain-Driven Design, is a practical software engineering guide that simplifies and restructures core DDD concepts.

goal.title: Goal
goal.description: With clear concepts and easy-to-follow principles, it prevents code from decaying into chaos, helping developers master complex systems and deliver sustainable rapid iteration.

value.title: Value Orientation
value.highlight: Keeping boundaries explicit is the most important thing.
value.description: Build models, rules, and implementations around boundaries so complexity stays organized.

items.title: Aggregate
items.description: An object cluster that independently maintains core business data and behavior with clear boundaries and consistency rules.

items.title: Domain Event
items.description: An object produced by aggregate behavior that reflects a business event, usually named in the past tense.

items.title: Domain Event Handler
items.description: Creates and emits the corresponding command based on a domain event.

items.title: Command
items.description: An object triggered by user action or system event to request a change in aggregate state.

items.title: Command Handler
items.description: Operates on an aggregate to fulfill business needs.

items.title: Query & Query Handler
items.description: Fetches aggregate data to satisfy user query requirements.

items.title: Scheduled Task
items.description: Runs at a specific time or interval, usually to emit commands that change aggregate state.

items.title: Integration Event
items.description: An event used to transfer information between systems, usually converted from a domain event.

items.title: Integration Event Handler
items.description: Handles integration events and emits corresponding commands, typically in the receiving system.

steps.title: Identify Aggregates
points: When you see a requirement to create x, x is likely an aggregate.
When x cannot exist alone and depends on another entity, define x as a child entity.

steps.title: Identify Commands & Handlers
points: If an operation needs to change aggregate state, define it as a command.
Commands are typically triggered by user actions, domain event handlers, or scheduled tasks.

steps.title: Identify Domain Events
points: Domain events are named in the past tense to show something important has happened.
Names should reflect business meaning, such as OrderCreated or CustomerAddressUpdated.

steps.title: Identify Domain Event Handlers
points: When a requirement says "after doing x, do y", use a domain event handler to trigger y.
Each handler should focus on a single domain event with clear responsibilities.

steps.title: Identify Queries
points: When users need to view aggregate data, define it as a query.
When business rules need aggregate data for decisions, define it as a query as well.

items.title: Aggregates
points: Aggregates cannot reference each other directly.
Aggregates do not share entities or reference other aggregates through child entities.
Objects inside an aggregate can only be changed through the aggregate root or child entity methods.
Aggregate property changes must be done through aggregate behavior (methods).

items.title: Domain Events
points: Domain events must be produced by aggregate behavior.

items.title: Command Handlers
points: A command handler can modify only one aggregate.

items.title: Event Handlers
points: An event handler can handle only one domain event.

items.title: Queries
points: Cross-aggregate join queries are not allowed.

items.question: How is CleanDDD related to Clean Architecture?
items.answer: CleanDDD has no direct relationship to Clean Architecture. While they share some similarities in code organization, their focus and goals differ, and the layering concepts are not the same. The "Clean" in CleanDDD emphasizes simplifying concepts and practical execution rather than a specific architecture style.

items.question: Will software built with CleanDDD perform poorly?
items.answer: No. Most business systems are I/O bound and read-heavy. CleanDDD enforces clear aggregate boundaries and disallows cross-aggregate direct operations, which leads to some redundant storage but reduces cross-aggregate data access, improving overall performance.
